entity.summary: The University of Edinburgh is listed as QS 2026 rank 34. The University of Edinburgh has 34 source-backed AI policy claim records from 11 official source attributions (including retained context and held sources). The public record preserves original-language evidence snippets, source URLs, snapshot hashes, confidence, and review state.

summary: The University of Edinburgh policy record updated with 34 reviewed claims across coursework, exams, disclosure, data security, available tools, and research. Central ELM gateway and Copilot chat in Edge documented; M365 Copilot full integration license confirmed unavailable; PGR thesis declaration, patient/clinical data restrictions, and registry appeal timescales recorded.

claims.claimText: The University of Edinburgh does not ban generative AI in postgraduate research, but its use is restricted for assessed work; researchers should consult supervisors and programme-level guidelines, should include a brief acknowledgment in the Declaration of Own Work if using AI for assessed research, and must adhere to publisher and funder rules.

evidence.evidenceSnippet:
The University does not ban the use of generative AI in your research, though its use is restricted for work assessed by the University.
Some programmes and disciplines may also restrict its use in other ways. Always check with your supervisors and any programme-level guidelines.
If you are considering using generative AI for research in conference papers, posters and publications, you should also consult any guidelines provided by the conference organiser or publisher and make any appropriate declarations.
If you are a funded student, check whether your funder stipulates any additional restrictions.

claims.claimText: The University of Edinburgh says students must not use third-party AI-based translation apps in class because they retain and distribute classroom recordings in violation of the Accessible and Inclusive Learning Policy.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The University’s Accessible and Inclusive Learning Policy allows you to make audio recordings of classes but does not allow you to share and distribute these recordings with a third party. AI-based translation apps retain and process recordings in a way that is not allowed in this policy. They can also negatively effect the group dynamic in tutorials and seminars. As a result, you must not use third-party AI-based translation apps in class.

claims.claimText: The University of Edinburgh encourages students to use ELM over external commercial AI platforms because its guidance states that data is not retained by third-party services to train models or for other purposes. March 2026 student guidance describes ELM as free to staff and students; another published entitlement page states discretionary School approval. Whether that approval condition still applies universally is not established by these sources.

evidence.evidenceSnippet:
The university encourages you to use ELM over other platforms such as GPT, DeepSeek, Grok etc for the following reasons:
In ELM your data is secure – it will not be retained by third party services to train their models or for any other purpose.
It is free to use for all staff and students, providing the same access for all and saving you money.

evidence.evidenceSnippet:
Many vendors are adding AI features to existing software. Treat these as new capabilities that require governance. Do not enable them by default. For Research use of AI follow your normal College Research Ethics Board process. Consider using the AI Impact Assessment guidance to frame decisions, and complete, where appropriate: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
Equality Impact Assessment (EQIA)

evidence.evidenceSnippet: All forms of academic misconduct are regarded as an offence and are punishable under the University’s Code of Student Conduct.
